newsitem.title: ECUADOR: 20 killed as U.S. jet crashes into Ecuadoran city.
newsitem.headline: 20 killed as U.S. jet crashes into Ecuadoran city.

text.p: At least 20 people were killed and 60 injured when an American-owned Boeing 707 cargo plane exploded over an Ecuadoran city and crashed into a densely-populated neighborhood, police said on Wednesday.

The Miami-bound plane, belonging to U.S. company Millium Air, exploded at 2240 Tuesday local time (0340 Wednesday GMT) shortly after taking off from the airport at the coastal city of Manta, 290 miles (480 km) southeast of the capital Quito.

An eye witness told local radio the jet was flying at low altitude over the poor central Manta district of Dolorosa when an engine apparently caught fire. He said the plane exploded and flaming wreckage rained down on houses and a church.
"We rushed out and we saw that it was ripping the roofs off all the houses," the man said. "Two houses just before ours fell over and collapsed just because of the force of the impact.
"Part of the wing ended up just near where we live. It had gone dragging all the houses down until it smashed into a restaurant. The owner was there and he was killed."
Police sub-lieutenent Marcelo Rocha told Reuters: "The engine caught fire and caused the accident. Up to now there are 20 dead and 60 wounded."
Rocha said the plane's four crew members, whose nationality he could not confirm, were all killed in the crash about six miles (10 km) from the airport.
Radio reported the jet was operated by Millium Air and had three American crew.
Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram declared a national day of mourning and was heading for the crash site to supervise resuce work and care of the victims, according to radio reports.
Mayor Jorge Zambrano said: "We have declared three days of mourning in the city of Manta in sympathy with the families affected by this accident."

Rescue teams from the Red Cross, civil defense and Ecuadoran Air Force were scouring the area for more dead or injured. Local radio reported that emergency services had temporarily laid out six corpses in a local park strewn with wreckage of the plane, while 14 more were taken to the local morgue.

Radio reports described how dozens of anguished people were waiting outside hospitals for news of their reletives and friends. An area covering five blocks of Dolorosa, in the middle of Manta, was littered with rubble and wreckage.
Local hospitals, who told Reuters they were treating patients for severe burns, said they were short of medication and equipment and called on the government to rush them more supplies.
The plane was carrying a cargo of frozen fish and flowers, according to the radio station.
